title: Affine localization comparison for the injective restriction source
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $U$ an open subscheme, $N$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], and $V$ an affine open. Write $R=\mathcal O_L(V)$ and $P=(j_*(N|_U))(V)$ for $j:U\hookrightarrow L$. Let $S\subseteq P$ be a finitely generated $R$-submodule and $p$ a prime ideal of $R$. Set $y=h_V.\mathrm{fromSpec}(p)$, the corresponding point of $V$. Assume N is finite on affine opens, its stalks outside U have depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-depth], and the restriction unit is injective on all opens. Write $a:N(V)\to P$ for this unit, assume $a(N(V))\subseteq S$, and let $K=a(N(V))\cap S$ viewed as a submodule of S. Then $K_p$ is finite over $R_p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. If $y\in U$, then $(S/K)_p=0$. If $y\notin U$, then $\operatorname{depth}_{R_p}(K_p)\ge2$. No depth conclusion about $(S/K)_p$ at boundary points is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0E9I (lemma-depth-2); Tag 0AV8 (lemma-reflexive-isomorphism), local-isomorphism case; Tags 01IA, 01HV and 01LC

proof.text: On the affine chart R is Noetherian. The FG hypothesis gives Module.Finite R S. Every submodule of S is finitely generated, so K and its prime localization are finite. Define b:M→S by codRestrict of the actual restriction unit using hMS, and c:M→K by codRestrict again. Injectivity of the unit makes c injective; membership in the comapped range makes c surjective. LinearEquiv.ofBijective and IsLocalizedModule.mapEquiv therefore identify M_p and K_p. These maps are constructed from the given unit, not chosen from an existence theorem.

Use lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization on N at the affine point y to localize the actual germ map. The affine ring stalk comparison identifies the stalk ring with R_p. Extend the germ localization equivalence to the localized scalar ring. A proved private semilinear depth-invariance lemma transports maximal ideals, regular sequences and lengths, with the zero-module case giving infinity. Thus depth(M_p)=depth(N_y); compose with the localized equivalence M_p≃K_p and apply the boundary depth hypothesis.

An open immersion into a locally Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact; it is quasi-separated. Apply pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh to G=j_*(N|U). At an interior point, the restricted unit is an isomorphism by the restriction adjunction, since its counit is an isomorphism. Naturality of restrictStalkNatIso transports this to an isomorphism on the original stalks. The module-stalk functor gives its linear map. Apply lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization to N and G; stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply identifies the localized unit with that stalk map by IsLocalizedModule.linearMap_ext. Therefore the localized unit M_p→P_p is surjective.

Localization preserves the injective subtype S→P and the factorizations of a through b and c, as checked on fractions with LocalizedModule.map_mk. Surjectivity M_p→P_p and injectivity S_p→P_p give surjectivity M_p→S_p, hence K_p→S_p. LocalizedModule.map_exact applied to subtype and mkQ identifies the kernel of the localized quotient map with the image of K_p. Since that image is all S_p, the quotient map is zero; since the quotient map is also surjective, every element of (S/K)_p is zero. This supplies Subsingleton and completes the conjunction.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0E9I and 0AV8, source-depth and interior-local-isomorphism comparison; Tags 01LC and 01HV for qcqs pushforward and affine stalk localization. Lean assembly uses the restriction adjunction and exactness of module localization.
